title: the trouble device's proofs run the host's bash, not the bare word bash
intention: Every trouble proof builds its bash argv from the host's bash (shutil.which on Windows), and an AST door proof over cairn/devices/trouble/proofs holds that no argv list starts with the bare word bash.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: git grep for a list literal headed by bash in cairn/devices/trouble found four sites: test_a_cli_clear_carries_the_hand.py:99, test_launcher_words_are_scripts.py:116,119, test_trouble_never_rides_the_bus.py:267
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof that runs another OS's shell on a box measures that shell, not the component; Law 4: held by a scan.
how: In the three proofs add a module _BASH that is shutil.which('bash') on nt and 'bash' elsewhere and use it as the argv head at the four sites. Add cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_no_trouble_proof_spawns_a_bare_bash.py, an AST scan of the trouble proofs for a Call whose first argument is a list headed by the string bash. Other reds in these proofs are other causes and are left alone.

clauses.claim: an AST scan of cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_*.py finds no Call whose first argument is a list headed by the string bash
the three edited proofs name the host's bash (a _BASH head) at their spawn sites

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.saw: git grep for a list literal headed by bash in cairn/devices/trouble found four sites: test_a_cli_clear_carries_the_hand.py:99, test_launcher_words_are_scripts.py:116,119, test_trouble_never_rides_the_bus.py:267
